A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EdiText study. Their complete main texts and appendices support reliable comparison of algorithms, equations, experiments, tables, and figures despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original toxicity, sentiment, and formality editing experiments, a human evaluation, and question-conditioned editing results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the human evaluation and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The LD4LG backbone and coarse, fine, and integrated editing procedures in Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. The expanded conditioning description documents existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use Implicit Toxicity for toxicity editing and Enron for sentiment and formality editing. The human evaluation and question-conditioned scenario already appear in v1's appendices and are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: ParaGuide and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct remain in the main comparisons, with Mix-and-Match DISC in Table 4 and DISC/HAM in Table 5.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the data splits, training budgets, control settings, evaluation metrics, and latent dimensions. The integrated-editing sweep and human-evaluation protocol are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The control-parameter sweeps, integrated-editing analysis, qualitative examples, and question-conditioned extension are retained. The new overview figure illustrates the existing method rather than reporting an additional analysis.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same MOS values and accompanying ± quantities. Both versions report 52 participants and 208 responses, with no added run counts, seed information, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All nine tables retain identical numerical results and qualitative examples. The main tradeoff plots, renumbered from Figure 2 to Figure 3, and the appendix Figure 4 also retain their plotted results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain their mathematical substance. v2 removes surplus delimiters from the loss expressions and clarifies the existing clean-latent reparameterization; these are explanatory and typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: coarse editing through SDEdit, fine editing through self-conditioning, and their integration for broad yet precise control.

C2.justification: Interpretations of editing range, retention–attribute tradeoffs, and context-conditioned editing remain unchanged. Both versions state the same limitations concerning backbone quality and the absence of an editing-specific training objective.

D1.justification: Expanded Appendix A.1 newly specifies that the learned attribute embedding is added to the timestep embedding and that self-conditioning is handled as separate context. This adds implementation detail for the existing algorithms.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shi et al. (2024), Simplified and Generalized Masked Diffusion for Discrete Data, to the introduction, related work, and references. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar corrections, clarifies the training and sampling explanation in Section 3.1, expands and retitles Appendix A.1, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the framework overview in Figure 2 and relocates existing tables and appendix displays. The main result plot becomes Figure 3 and the prompt template becomes Figure 5; existing display contents and designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new overview figure and expanded Appendix A.1 make the existing framework easier to understand and clarify how attribute and self-conditioning inputs enter the model. Clearer exposition and corrected equation delimiters provide additional modest benefits. These targeted documentation improvements support a limited overall quality gain.
